three seasons.{{Cite web | title = Charles Jenkins stats | publisher = [[ESPN]] | date = 2010 | url = http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=31911 | accessdate = 13 May 2010}} He is Hofstra's all-time leading scorer, breaking [[Antoine Agudio]] (2,286) set in 2007–08, and will graduate as the second leading scorer in [[Colonial Athletic Association]] history behind [[Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Famer]] [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]], who scored 2,669 points at [[Navy Midshipmen men's basketball|Navy]].{{Cite web| last = Satriano| first = David| title = Hofstra's Jenkins shows Pride in finale| work = [[New York Post]]| publisher = nypost.com| date = February 27, 2011| url = http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/college/basketball/jenkins_shows_pride_in_finale_j3EXFwDefT9IDy4t2f8JGJ | accessdate = March 6, 2011}} Jenkins had his jersey retired by Hofstra prior to his final home game of his senior season, making him the fourth player in school history to be so honored, and the first to have it retired while still active. ==Early life== A native of [[Queens]], [[New York City]], Jenkins played high school basketball at [[Springfield Gardens High School]] for three seasons. As a senior in 2005–06, he averaged 21.1 points, 7.2 assists and 5.1 rebounds en route to a ''[[New York Post]]'' selection to the All-New York City Team. ==Hofstra University== ===Freshman=== After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his [[true freshman]] season of 2006–07, Jenkins began competing for the [[Hofstra Pride]] in 2007–08. He played in 29 games and averaged 15.0 points and 4.6 rebounds, led his team in free throw percentage (78.0), and finished 10th in the [[Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA) in scoring (first among freshmen). Jenkins was named the CAA Rookie of the Year, Metropolitan New York Rookie of the Year and to the Third Team All-Metropolitan New York. ===Sophomore=== In 2008–09, Jenkins averaged 19.7 points and 4.8 rebounds in 32 games played. In the last game of the regular season against [[UNCW Seahawks men's basketball|UNC Wilmington]], he surpassed the 1,000-point milestone, joining Agudio as the only two sophomores to reach 1,000 points prior to their junior seasons. At the season's end, his 1,065 points stood 47 points more than Agudio's pace at the end of his respective sophomore season. Jenkins garnered numerous awards for his year. Among them was the coveted [[Haggerty Award]], which is an award given annually to the greater New York Metropolitan area's best [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] men's basketball player.{{Cite web | last = Sass | first = Max | title = Charles Jenkins wins second-straight Haggerty Award | publisher = ''The Chronicle'' | date = 22 April 2010 | url = http://www.hofstrachronicle.com/sports/charles-jenkins-wins-second-straight-haggerty-award-1.1379128 | accessdate = 13 May 2010}} He became just the fifth sophomore overall (and first since [[Ron Artest]] in 1998–99) to earn it in the 73-year history of the award to that point. ===Junior=== As a junior in 2009–10, Jenkins once again increased most of his season averages. He scored 20.6 points, grabbed 4.5 rebounds, dished out 3.9 assists and shot 40.9% from three-point range. On November 30, 2009, in an 84–80 win versus [[Fairfield Stags men's basketball|Fairfield]], he scored a career high 38 points on 12-for-17 shooting and went 9-for-9 in free throw attempts. Although the Pride would finish the year with a 19–15 overall record, Jenkins' personal play was good enough to make him the [[Colonial Athletic Association Men's Basketball Player of the Year]].{{Cite web| title = Hofstra's Jenkins Earns CAA Men's Basketball Player of the Year Honors | work = Men's Basketball News | publisher = [[Colonial Athletic Association]] | date = 4 March 2010 | url = http://www.caasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=8500&ATCLID=204901228 | format = Press release | accessdate = 13 May 2010}} Additionally, he became just the ninth repeat winner of the Haggerty Award.{{Cite web | title = Hofstra's Jenkins Repeats as Haggerty Award winner | work = Men's Basketball News | publisher = [[Colonial Athletic Association]] | date = 21 April 2010 | url = http://www.caasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=8500&ATCLID=204933411 | format = Press release | accessdate = 13 May 2010}} ===Senior=== Jenkins became just the third player all-time to win the Haggerty Award three times, joining [[Jim McMillian]] ([[Columbia Lions men's basketball|Columbia]], 1968–70) and [[Chris Mullin (basketball)|Chris Mullin]] ([[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]], 1983–85), both of whom later achieved great success at the [[NBA]] and/or [[Summer Olympic Games|Olympic]] levels of competition. ==Personal== Jenkins has one brother and one sister. He cites [[Pearl Washington]] as his favorite athlete, and prior to selecting Hofstra he had also been recruited by [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] and [[Liberty Flames men's basketball|Liberty]]. ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== *[http://www.gohofstra.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=22200&ATCLID=3716182 Hofstra biography] {{Colonial Athletic Association Men's Basketball Player of the Year}} {{Chip Hilton Player of the Year}} {{Haggerty Award}} {{Persondata | NAME = Jenkins, Charles | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = | DATE OF BIRTH = 28 February 1989 | PLACE OF BIRTH = | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Jenkins, Charles}} [[Category:1989 births]] [[Category:American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York]] [[Category:Hofstra Pride men's basketball players]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Queens]] [[Category:Shooting guards]]
